name: Santali
note: Has its own Ol Chiki script, created in 1925, and is a scheduled language of India.

name: Mundari
note: A Munda language of the Chotanagpur plateau.

name: Ho
note: Written in the Warang Citi script devised by Lako Bodra.

name: Kurukh (Oraon)
note: A North Dravidian language, spoken far from the other Dravidian languages.

name: Gondi
note: Has its own scripts, including Gunjala Gondi lipi and Masaram Gondi.

name: Bhili
note: The language of the Bhil communities, among the largest tribal groups in India.

name: Khasi
note: An Austroasiatic language in a north-east region where most languages are Tibeto-Burman.

name: Garo (A·chik)
note: Spoken by the A·chik people of the Garo Hills.

name: Mizo
note: The most widely used language of Mizoram.

name: Bodo (Boro)
note: A scheduled language of India, spoken mainly in Assam.

name: Kokborok
note: The main language of the Tripuri people and an official language of Tripura.

name: Adi
note: A Tani language. The Donyi-Polo faith honours the sun (Donyi) and the moon (Polo).

name: Ao Naga
note: One of the main languages of Nagaland, with Chungli and Mongsen varieties.

name: Lepcha (Rong)
note: Speakers call themselves and their language Rong.

name: Jaunsari
note: A Western Pahari language of Jaunsar-Bawar in Dehradun district.

name: Kui (Khond)
note: The language of the Kondh community, mostly written in the Odia script.

name: Koya
note: A Gondi-related Dravidian language spoken along the Godavari river valley.

name: Sora (Savara)
note: A Munda language with its own Sorang Sompeng script.

name: Angami Naga
note: Spoken by the Angami people around Kohima; the Tenyidie variety is widely used.

name: Nyishi
note: A Tani language and one of the most widely spoken languages of Arunachal Pradesh.
